title: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
problem: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs with trillion-scale parameters must be offloaded to CPU/disk memory when GPU VRAM is insufficient, but each expert's compute time per token is shorter than the I/O time to load it, creating large pipeline bubbles that negate the benefit of overlapping I/O and computation.
method: Klotski introduces an expert-aware multi-batch pipeline that maintains multiple batches in flight simultaneously and schedules which experts to prefetch and compute based on expert routing decisions across batches. By batching tokens that activate the same expert across multiple concurrent requests, Klotski increases per-expert compute volume to exceed I/O time, eliminating pipeline bubbles. The system tracks expert access patterns across batches and uses an expert prefetching scheduler that co-optimizes I/O and compute assignment to saturate both the memory bus and compute units.

title: CND-IDS: Continual Novelty Detection for Intrusion Detection Systems
problem: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems struggle with two critical challenges: streaming network traffic that changes over time, and the lack of labels for novel (zero-day) attacks.
method: CND-IDS combines a continually-updated learning-based feature extractor that adapts feature representations to new system data with a novelty detector using PCA reconstruction to identify anomalies, eliminating dependence on attack labels.

title: E-morphic: Scalable Equality Saturation for Structural Exploration in Logic Synthesis
problem: Technology-independent logic synthesis produces a single canonical circuit structure; missing opportunities for alternative structures that may optimize better for specific technology mappings.
method: E-morphic: equality saturation framework for resynthesis after technology-independent optimization; direct e-graph-circuit conversion; solution-space pruning; simulated annealing for e-graph extraction; enables parallel structural exploration before technology mapping.

title: S-SYNC: Shuttle and Swap Co-Optimization in Quantum Charge-Coupled Devices
problem: In Quantum Charge-Coupled Device (QCCD) trapped-ion architectures, coherent qubit shuttling across segmented electrode arrays increases thermal motion and consistently forces additional SWAP operations to restore qubit connectivity, significantly extending circuit execution time and degrading application success rates.
method: S-SYNC is a compiler that co-optimizes shuttle and SWAP counts simultaneously by exploiting QCCD-specific topology properties. It formulates QCCD routing as a static topology problem and incorporates generic SWAP gate insertion as a first-class operation alongside shuttle moves, rather than treating them independently. Scheduling heuristics then jointly minimize both operation types across the circuit, balancing the thermal motion cost of shuttling against the gate overhead of SWAPs. The compiler is evaluated across multiple QCCD topologies and initial qubit mapping strategies.

title: RADiT: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion Transformer Acceleration Leveraging Timestep Similarity
problem: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) require multiple iterative sampling timesteps with redundant computations across consecutive steps, leading to high latency and energy consumption during inference.
method: RADiT identifies data redundancy via blockwise input feature evaluation and skips redundant computations by reusing results from consecutive timesteps. Dynamic Threshold Scaling Module (DTSM) and Compress and Compare Unit (CCU) minimize accuracy degradation while maximizing computational efficiency during redundancy detection.

title: Enabling Efficient Mobile Tracing with BTrace
problem: Existing mobile tracing tools use distributed per-core or per-thread buffers that prioritize performance but have a high probability of missing crucial trace events in smartphone scenarios, where event ordering and completeness are critical for diagnosing stability issues.
method: BTrace introduces a mobile-optimized tracing design that addresses the incompleteness problem of per-core/per-thread distributed buffers by redesigning the buffer management and synchronization strategy for smartphone workloads. The system uses a centralized or coordinated buffering approach that preserves event completeness while maintaining acceptable performance overhead, tailored to the smartphone system software stack.

title: Automatic Tracing in Task-Based Runtime Systems
problem: In task-based parallel runtime systems, dependence analysis becomes a performance bottleneck when task granularity is fine, and existing tracing techniques that memoize this analysis require brittle manual annotations by programmers that are difficult to apply to programs built from composing independent library components.
method: Apophenia automatically discovers traces in task-based runtime systems through a series of dynamic string analyses applied to the stream of tasks issued by the application. It identifies repeated program fragments online by treating the task stream as a string and detecting periodicity, then memoizes the dependence analysis for those fragments. The system requires no programmer annotation and integrates with existing task-based runtimes by intercepting the task issue API.

title: Invited: EDA for Heterogeneous Integration
problem: Heterogeneous integration (chiplet-based systems) demands new EDA methodologies beyond traditional monolithic chip design. Chiplet disaggregation, multi-physics analysis, physical design for substrates, and interchiplet communication optimization remain open challenges.
method: The paper outlines four key EDA areas: (1) chiplet disaggregation and system-technology co-optimization methods to map designs onto chiplets; (2) multiphysics and multiscale analyses spanning fast ML-driven early-stage analysis to signoff-quality thermomechanical simulation; (3) physical design techniques for chiplet placement, routing, and power delivery on substrates; (4) infrastructure including chiplet libraries, data formats, and standards.

title: CHORD: Composable Hybrid Optical Reconfigurable Diffractive Framework For Optical Neural Network
problem: Diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs) offer ultra-parallel, high-efficiency computing via freespace light propagation, but lack reconfigurability due to fixed post-fabrication optical structures, limiting practical deployment for dynamic AI workloads.
method: CHORD combines composable hybrid optical/photonic design with full-system learnability. Fixed fabricated optical hardware is repurposed through differentiable learning of system variables, achieving reconfigurability. Hybrid design leverages integrated photonic reconfigurability with free-space diffractive ultra-parallelism.

title: SynCircuit: Automated Generation of New Synthetic RTL Circuits Can Enable Big Data in Circuits
problem: Scarcity of circuit design data limits AI-assisted IC design. Existing generative models cannot reliably generate valid HDL circuits with correct digital logic.
method: Uses diffusion-based generative model to generate directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) representing circuits, applies constraint refinement to enforce logic validity, and employs Monte Carlo tree search to optimize redundancy in the generated graphs.

title: MemSens: Significantly Reducing Memory Overhead in Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis Using Novel Error-Bounded Lossy Compression
problem: Adjoint sensitivity analysis requires storing all state vectors and Jacobian matrices at every time step for gradient computation, leading to prohibitive memory costs for large-scale dynamic systems and long simulations.
method: Proposes error-bounded lossy compression of state information that exploits spatiotemporal characteristics of circuit simulation data. Combines specialized compression algorithms with stringent error control mechanisms to reduce stored state volume while maintaining adjoint solution accuracy.

title: NoiseZO: RRAM Noise-Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization for Efficient Forward-Only Training
problem: RRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) training requires gradient computation overhead; RRAM write noise complicates training convergence.
method: NoiseZO maps neural networks to dual RRAM arrays and exploits intrinsic RRAM write noise as zeroth-order perturbations for gradient-free training; fine-grained perturbation control enhances accuracy; training requires only two forward passes per update.

title: ReSBM: Region-based Scale and Minimal-Level Bootstrapping Management for FHE via Min-Cut
problem: In RNS-CKKS fully homomorphic encryption, repeated homomorphic multiplications escalate ciphertext scale and consume multiplicative levels, requiring expensive bootstrapping to restore capacity; existing compile-time approaches do not efficiently minimize the number and placement of bootstrapping operations, leading to excess overhead in encrypted ML inference.
method: ReSBM partitions the FHE computation graph into regions using a min-cut graph algorithm that identifies the minimal set of bootstrapping insertion points needed to prevent ciphertext level overflow. Within each region, scale management is handled to keep multiplicative levels within bounds. The min-cut formulation finds a provably minimal-bootstrapping schedule at compile time, reducing the number of costly bootstrapping operations without sacrificing correctness. This is coupled with region-level scale assignment to prevent capacity overflow throughout encrypted inference.

title: Finding the Pareto Frontier of Low-Precision Data Formats and MAC Architecture for LLM Inference
problem: Complex design space of low-precision data formats (integer, floating-point, posit, LNS) and MAC implementations (conventional and block-quantized) makes it difficult to identify optimal area/power/accuracy tradeoffs for LLM inference.
method: Evaluates 35,000+ MAC designs spanning multiple data formats (INT, FP, posit, LNS, MX, VSQ) and design parameters (inner product size, accumulation width). Each MAC is evaluated for area, power (in TOPs/W), and numerical accuracy (signal-to-quantization noise ratio). Pareto-optimal designs are identified across the design space.

title: PASK: Cold Start Mitigation for Inference with Proactive and Selective Kernel Loading on GPUs
problem: DNN inference suffers from significant cold-start latency when models are spawned from scratch (spot serving, serverless, edge computing), caused by kernel loading overhead where DL primitive libraries (cuDNN, MIOpen) prepare GPU code objects before execution.
method: PASK is a kernel loading and reuse middleware that replaces reactive kernel scheduling with proactive loading: interleaves code loading, kernel issuing, and GPU computation to hide loading latency and improve hardware utilization. Kernels are categorically organized in a cache to enable efficient kernel reuse across DNN layers; the system recycles applicable kernels for operators instead of invoking new kernels per layer.

title: BPUFuzzer: Effective Fuzz Testing for Branching Transient Execution Vulnerabilities of RISC-V CPU
problem: Transient execution vulnerabilities (e.g., Spectre) in CPU branch prediction units are difficult to detect through traditional testing; existing fuzz testing approaches lack effective testcase generation for complex control flows and data extraction from vast RTL state spaces.
method: BPUFuzzer uses control flow graph-based testcase generation with anomaly detection to explore complex program flows and deliberately selects testcases using fitness and coverage metrics to discover transient execution vulnerabilities. It extracts essential data from hardware states to guide testcase selection.
